name: Fujicolor C200
notes: Fujicolor C200, Fujifilm Product Information Bulletin, plots on page 6 (nos. 18, 19 and 21), a scanned page (raster image, about 600 dpi); the curves were traced from hand-placed hints (for the characteristic-curve and dye plots the hints were then re-set on the first trace so that they sit on the curves). Process printed on the plots: CN-16. Date taken from the print code 17.05-BX next to the reference number in the footer (no other date printed).
Speed: daylight ISO 200/24 degrees; 3200 K tungsten ISO 50/18 degrees with Wratten 80A (Fuji LBB-12). No Log H Ref is printed (log_h_ref null).

curves: x is log H in lux-seconds as printed (daylight, 1/125 s); all three curves are solid and never touch (D-min plateaus about 0.73 b, 0.43 g, 0.14 r; the curves end at log H about 0.25 b, 0.38 g, 0.31 r). The last point of a line can lie up to one 0.05 step beyond the drawn end (flat extrapolation by the tool).

sensitivity: the y axis has NO numbers, only a double arrow marking 1.0 between two horizontal rules. y is therefore set to 1.0 on the upper rule and 0.0 on the lower rule: the zero is arbitrary, only differences between points and between layers are meaningful. Sensitivity = reciprocal of the exposure in J/cm2 giving density 1.0 above D-min (Status M, CN-16).

sensitivity: all three curves are plain solid lines that cross each other (blue/green near 500 nm, green/red near 580 nm); each layer ends in a near-vertical drop (blue ends about 510 nm, green starts about 460 nm and ends about 600 nm, red starts about 565 nm and ends about 680 nm); the tool keeps one y per x, so the last few nm of the drops are approximated, and the first/last sample on the 5 nm grid can be a flat extension of up to 5 nm.

dyes: the plot is not of separate cyan/magenta/yellow dyes but of two curves, Mid-scale Density (mid; typical densities for a mid-scale neutral subject) and Minimum Density (min; D-min), 400-720 nm, y = spectral diffuse density as printed (0-2.5).

Grain: diffuse RMS granularity value 4 (micro-densitometer aperture 48 um diameter, sample density 1.0 above minimum density; Fujifilm measurement, not comparable with colour reversal film). The plots look the same as those of Superia X-TRA 400 (AF3-0217E) but the curves differ slightly.
